supplied_text: Concurrent grievance-reference verification. The previous grievance identifier implementation was replaced with a PostgreSQL sequence-backed reference generator. A direct database concurrency test was executed using PostgreSQL 16 pgbench with 50 simultaneous clients, 8 worker threads and 10 transactions per client, producing 500 attempted inserts. All 500 transactions completed successfully with zero failed transactions. Average transaction latency was 17.777 ms. A post-test uniqueness query across the accumulated verification dataset returned 1,200 grievance rows and 1,200 distinct grievance_number values, confirming zero collisions. This test deliberately bypassed HTTP rate limiting to isolate the database mechanism that caused the original race condition; it therefore verifies database-level concurrency safety rather than end-to-end API throughput.
scope: Direct database mechanism; HTTP rate limiting bypassed; not an end-to-end API throughput result or whole sequence-range proof.
independent_prior_observation: fix_scope_inspection.json captured 1,200 sequence-format rows plus 3,354 legacy-format rows; 1,200 refers to the verification dataset, not the entire historical table.
